prime.problem: A course sized by its video length (18 h 38 min) gets planned as two weekends and falls behind from the first lecture. And a laptop plan that doesn't know which run needs a GPU either stalls at the last lecture or rents hardware that sits idle for weeks.
prime.fits: Second card of the series map. It turns the loop from How to use this course into hours and sittings, and it summarises the setup card in the toolkit (z2h-1) that every lab depends on.
expect: the one-environment setup and its check
video × 2–3 as the real time cost
prime.goal: Build the environment, budget the series in hours and weeks, and say which single run needs a rented GPU, what it costs and why.

attend: Why does the setup check print a seeded random draw, and what would a different draw tell you?
Where does the × 2–3 multiplier come from, and what would push you toward the high end?
Why are losses treated as exact but times only as guides?
What ratio makes the GPT-2 training run impossible on the laptop but fine on 8×A100?

must: Same Python, torch 2.14, device and seed as the labs → the same outputs as "You should see" → a mismatch means your code, not your setup
Typing along, pausing and doing Study panels → roughly 2–3× the video → 18 h 38 min becomes about 37–56 h → plan weeks, not weekends
10.00B tokens ÷ about 1,300 tok/s on the M3 → about 89 days; ÷ about 1.5M tok/s on 8×A100 → about 2 h → rent only for that one run (README: ~$10)
Timing depends on machine load, but losses and parameter counts don't → trust the losses exactly and treat times as ranges → start the long runs before a break
elevated: makemore runs on cpu, not mps → the CPU generator reproduces the notebook's seeded numbers → the L1–L6 outputs match the video, where the mps generator would not
reference: the install commands and package list
the video length of each lecture

compress.prompt: Course-level compress: from memory, sketch the schedule as three bands (laptop-fast lectures, laptop-slow runs, rented GPU) and put every course in one. Then write the one division that explains why GPT-2 training is in the GPU band.
checklist: laptop-fast: z2h-1 to z2h-4 and z2h-9 (seconds to about a minute)
laptop-slow: z2h-5 to z2h-7 (1–5 min), the full gpt.py (about 2–2.5 h) and the HellaSwag eval (about 17 min)

retrieve.q: Explain what the setup check proves, and why it matters for every "You should see" in the series.
answer: the right Python and torch version, and that the device (mps) is available
the seeded CPU draw matches Karpathy's [0.7081, 0.3542, 0.1054]
so any later mismatch is in your code, not your environment

retrieve.q: Walk through how you'd turn the WaveNet lecture (56 min 21 s) into a plan: hours, sittings and the longest run.
answer: at 2-hour sittings, about one sitting at the midpoint
longest runs: the final model 147 s and the BatchNorm bug lab 301 s (serial)

retrieve.q: You could rent a GPU for all of Lecture 9 or just its final run. What does each choice cost, and what could go wrong with renting only at the end?
answer: the whole lecture: paying for 8–12 h of mostly typing time
the end only: about 1–2 h at about $10 (README)
the risk at the end: a bug found on the rented box wastes paid time, so prove the --quick run and the eval on the laptop first

compare.q: This card and the setup card both cover setup. What does the setup card explain that this one only summarises, and when do you need the full version?
answer: the setup card explains each line of the check, the cpu vs mps generators and the matmul sanity check
this card keeps only the commands and the pass condition
you need the full version when the check fails, or when you add the packages for later lectures (graphviz, transformers, datasets)

compare.q: The schedule says 8×A100 does 10B tokens in about 2 h. What does the big-batch card add about how eight GPUs share one run, and what doesn't carry over to your laptop?
answer: DDP: 8 processes, each with its own micro-batches, averaging gradients with an all-reduce
gradient accumulation reaches the 2<sup>19</sup>-token batch when memory can't hold it at once
on the laptop, accumulation still works (the lab does it), but you have one device, so there's no speedup

predict.q: Suppose the rented node were 8×H100 instead of 8×A100, and it ran the same script at about twice the tokens per second. Before computing: would you expect the cost of the run to halve, stay the same, or something else?
predict.answer: Not necessarily halve: the time halves (about 1 h instead of about 2 h), but an H100 node usually rents for more per hour than an A100 node, so the cost depends on the price ratio. Roughly, cost = hours × hourly rate, so it comes down only if the rate less than doubles. For comparison, nanochat's README prices an 8×H100 node at about $24/h.

apply.task: Make your own schedule. Pick a weekly number of hours you can really keep. Using the table, compute how many weeks the nine lectures take at × 2 and at × 3, and put the long runs (full gpt.py, the HellaSwag eval) where you'll be away from the laptop.
apply.done: At 6 h/week your range is 37.3 ÷ 6 ≈ 6.2 to 55.9 ÷ 6 ≈ 9.3 weeks; at your own number, you have a range in weeks plus two named slots for the long runs.
apply.hint: The total video is 18.64 h; × 2 = 37.3 h, × 3 = 55.9 h.
